feedback: REJECT — the RM never makes the task's 'pick it up on your very next move' clause load-bearing, so it pays the full success reward to trajectories that violate it. Core flaw: after a fall the machine sits in u1 for exactly one step; (u1, !holding_box) -> u0 with no reward silently cancels the pending obligation, after which a late pickup from u0 (covered by else, 0) followed by (u0, at_exit & holding_box) -> u2 still pays 1.0. Concrete violating trace: fall at step 4 -> u1; step 5 done (0, back to u0); late pickup whenever convenient; walk to the exit holding the box -> 1.0, although the task requires an immediate pickup after every fall. The 0.1-vs-0 distinction on the step after a fall is shaping only: since at most two falls occur per episode, a violator forfeits at most 0.2 while keeping the 1.0, so the constraint is cheap to ignore — a semantic-fidelity and reward-safety failure, and exactly the explicit regression (a mistake that permanently forfeits success) this task requires and the candidate omits. Required structure (description only, not a rewrite): keep u0 and (u1, holding_box) -> u0 with +0.1, but route (u1, !holding_box) to a new sticky violation state with a per-state else self-loop and all-zero rewards, so that exiting from that state is never rewarded (the else self-loop holds it there; the episode ends with 0). This is well-defined for this domain: after any real fall the box is always pickable on the next move because the fall turns the agent to face it, falls never occur on the episode-ending step so u1 always resolves on a real step, and (u1, at_exit & holding_box) is impossible since pickup does not move the agent and a fall cannot coincide with the exit step. Secondary issues: (a) (u1, else) -> u1 is dead code because (u1, holding_box) and (u1, !holding_box) jointly cover every assignment — a compactness flaw that also exposes the one-step-blip misunderstanding of u1; (b) several listed transitions ((u0, box_fell) -> u1, (u1, !holding_box) -> u0, (u1, else) -> u1, (u2, else) -> u2) have no REWARD_FUNCTION entries — add explicit 0s if the paper format requires a reward for every declared transition, otherwise state the 0 default; (c) exiting empty-handed falls through the u0 else with 0, which is acceptable, though an explicit failure sink would be cleaner. Positives: the FINAL_STATES header is present and its state declared (so no header-based rejection); the final condition at_exit & holding_box correctly encodes 'take the box to the exit' with the siren rightly irrelevant (siren_ringing and switch_toggled are covered by else self-loops in all three states); the 0.1 progress reward is bounded and unexploitable (falls are scheduler-driven, at most two per episode, and pickups from u0 pay nothing); and the step-after-fall mechanics are right, since holding_box on the step after box_fell holds iff the agent picked up on that very move.

def siren_ringing(env): return env.siren_ringing
def switch_toggled(env): return "toggle" in env.events_this_step
def holding_box(env): return env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "box"
def box_fell(env): return "fall" in env.events_this_step
